title: Pee Wee Russell and the start of Pee Wee and Art's Back Room
summary: Hodes tells how he and Pee Wee Russell, both broke, walked to find a job in 1949. The union let them run the club for six months before the delegation spoke.

venues.name: Pee Wee and Art's Back Room

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so I was at one place six months before the delegation came up and said to me, we know you're there, we've been knowing you're there. You haven't come up and told us, but we know you're there. We figured to give you a chance to get this thing started. And that was Pee Wee and Art's Back Room. Gave us six months.
Back Room. Pee Wee Russell and I started a club called Pee Wee and Art's Back Room. We're both on our bottoms, no money, walking the streets.

This was 1949. It was the Riviera Lounge. Kitty corner from Nick's. And Pee Wee said to me as we -- we didn't have money to walk from 56th Street to the Village -- to drive. The fare was five cents, something like that. So we couldn't spare it.
1949. So we walked. It might have been ten cents. But it was very minimal. And we walked there.
